links.outcome: Change in mean systolic blood pressure at 180 days, CDS vs usual care (silent mode)
links.effect: Mean SBP change -14.6 vs -11.7 mm Hg (P = .005). BP control did not differ (50.4% vs 47.1%). Aligned actions 49.9% vs 34.6% (P < .001).
links.quote: From the linear mixed model, there was a statistically significant difference in mean SBP change in the intervention group compared with the usual care group (change, -14.6 [95% CI, -13.1 to -16.0] mm Hg vs -11.7 [-10.2 to -13.1] mm Hg; P = .005).

unlisted_practices: Behavioral economics and human-centered design applied to CDS recommendations
Tailored evidence-based CDS recommendations for hypertension in CKD, tested in a randomized trial

screen.reason: The study evaluates a traditional rules-based computerized clinical decision support (CDS) system based on clinical practice guidelines and behavioral economics, not an AI, machine learning, or foundation model technology.
